documents.unit: ACU Library (Faculty Guide: AI and ChatGPT)
documents.title: Faculty Guide: AI and ChatGPT: Academic Integrity
documents.summary: A library faculty guide that tells instructors to define acceptable AI use in their syllabi and lists what such a statement should cover. It also gives MLA and APA citation formats for AI and three sample syllabus statements (AI required, prohibited, permitted with permission). It sets no rule of its own for ACU students.
documents.stance_why: The guide says "Best practice is to define what is acceptable and not acceptable in your class" and offers three example statements (required, prohibited, use-with-permission) rather than one rule, so the decision is left to instructors: delegates, with the three examples as tiers.

units.why: The MLA format line states what an AI citation must contain: "Name of AI tool, version of AI tool, Company, Date of chat, URL." That is tool, version and date detail, so P25 rather than the generic disclosure type P24.
units.anchor: Name of AI tool, version of AI tool, Company, Date of chat, URL.

units.why: "If you create a shareable link to the chat transcript, include that instead of the tool's URL" tells students what to put in the citation, so it is a citation-detail rule (P25) about the transcript link.
units.anchor: If you create a shareable link to the chat transcript, include that instead

units.why: "MLA also recommends acknowledging when you used the tool in a note or your text" asks for acknowledgment of AI use in the submission, so P24 (disclose with each submission), modality should because it is a recommendation.
units.anchor: acknowledging when you used the tool in a note or your text
units.policy: MLA recommends acknowledging when you used the AI tool in a note or in your text.

units.why: The same sentence recommends "verifying any sources or citations the tool supplies"; this is verification of AI output (P31), distinct from the acknowledgment rule above.
units.anchor: verifying any sources or citations the tool supplies

units.why: APA guidance says "It may be worthwhile to include the chat's transcript as an appendix to your project." That asks students to keep and submit the transcript, so P26, with modality may because the wording is optional.
units.anchor: include the chat's transcript as an appendix to your project
units.frag_start: It may be worthwhile to include
units.frag_end: as an appendix to your project.

units.why: "Use the company as the author, not the tool's name" and the bracketed prompt description are detailed citation requirements naming prompt and company, so P25.
units.anchor: Include a brief description of the chat indicating the prompts in square brackets.
units.frag_start: Use the company as the author,

units.why: For chats that are not retrievable, "only include an in-text citation and do not include an entry in the references list" and cite as personal communication. It specifies how AI is cited, so P25.
units.anchor: only include an in-text citation and do not include an entry in the references list

units.why: "Conversations with students reveal that they are uncertain about what levels of AI use are appropriate" and "our campus definitions of plagiarism and cheating may not be clear" give the reason for defining policy. No type covers this problem statement about unclear campus definitions, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: our campus definitions of plagiarism and cheating may not be clear
units.uncovered_note: States that students are uncertain about acceptable AI use and that campus definitions of plagiarism and cheating may not cover AI; the rationale for instructors to define expectations.

units.why: "Best practice is to define what is acceptable and not acceptable in your class. Be transparent upfront." tells instructors to state AI expectations to students at the start; P09 fits (communicating expectations) better than P04 because it concerns stating rules, not who decides.
units.anchor: define what is acceptable and not acceptable in your class

units.why: "Your policy should include these considerations: Under what circumstances AI use is permitted or forbidden" tells instructors that the syllabus statement should say when AI is permitted or forbidden, so P09.
units.anchor: Under what circumstances AI use is permitted or forbidden
units.policy: A syllabus AI policy should state under what circumstances AI use is permitted or forbidden.

units.why: The policy should include "How students should cite or credit AI", i.e. a citation requirement to be stated in the syllabus. The rule being set is that students cite AI, so P24.
units.anchor: How students should cite or credit AI
units.policy: A syllabus AI policy should say how students should cite or credit AI.

units.why: "A warning about the technology's tendency toward hallucination (i.e., deceptive data)" is a warning that AI output can be wrong, so P31.
units.anchor: A warning about the technology’s tendency toward hallucination
units.policy: A syllabus AI policy should include a warning about the technology's tendency toward hallucination.

units.why: "clear rules regarding students' accountability for AI output" asks for rules that students are responsible for AI output; P29 (students own what they submit) fits.
units.anchor: clear rules regarding students’ accountability for AI output
units.policy: A syllabus AI policy should include clear rules regarding students' accountability for AI output.

units.why: "A notice about using AI ethically and responsibly" is a general ethics notice with no specific content, so P53 (ethical concerns) is the closest type.
units.anchor: A notice about using AI ethically and responsibly
units.policy: A syllabus AI policy should include a notice about using AI ethically and responsibly.

units.why: "the need to use AI as a tool to learn, not just to produce content" says AI should support learning and not replace the work; P32 (student stays the problem-solver) rather than P41 since it is directive, not a skill-building argument.
units.anchor: use AI as a tool to learn, not just to produce content
units.frag_start: Discussion of the need to use
units.policy: A syllabus AI policy should discuss the need to use AI as a tool to learn, not just to produce content.

units.why: "I expect you to use AI (e.g., ChatGPT and image generation tools) in this class" makes AI use expected by default, so P02; unit stance encourage. It is an example statement shown to faculty.
units.anchor: I expect you to use AI (e.g., ChatGPT and image generation tools) in this class
units.frag_start: I expect you to use AI

units.why: "some assignments will require it" makes AI use mandatory on some assignments; P02 covers expected use, unit stance require.
units.anchor: some assignments will require it

units.why: "Learning to use AI is an emerging skill and I provide tutorials on how to use them" presents AI use as a skill the course teaches, so P44.
units.anchor: Learning to use AI is an emerging skill and I provide tutorials

units.why: "I am happy to meet and help you with these tools during office hours or after class" is instructor support for learning AI tools in the course, so P44 (course teaches AI use).
units.anchor: I am happy to meet and help you with these tools during office hours

units.why: "You will need to refine your prompts in order to get good outcomes" tells students that effective AI use takes effort and iteration, so P44 (teach effective AI use).
units.anchor: You will need to refine your prompts in order to get good outcomes.

units.why: "Don't trust anything it says. If it gives you a number or fact, assume it is wrong unless you ... can check with another source" tells students to verify AI output, so P31.
units.anchor: Don’t trust anything it says.
units.frag_end: It works best for topics you understand.

units.why: "You will be responsible for any errors or omissions provided by the tool" places responsibility for AI output on the student, so P29.
units.anchor: You will be responsible for any errors or omissions provided by the tool.
units.frag_start: You will be responsible for any

units.why: "Please include a paragraph at the end of any assignment that uses AI explaining what you used the AI for" requires an AI statement with each submission, so P24.
units.anchor: include a paragraph at the end of any assignment that uses AI
units.frag_start: AI is a tool, but one
units.policy: Students include a paragraph at the end of any assignment that uses AI explaining what they used the AI for.

units.why: The same paragraph must say "what prompts you used to get the results", a prompt-detail requirement distinct from the statement itself, so P25.
units.anchor: what prompts you used to get the results
units.frag_start: AI is a tool, but one

units.why: "Failure to do so is in violation of academic honesty policies" makes nondisclosure itself the violation, so P28 (rather than P36, since the point is disclosure).
units.anchor: Failure to do so is in violation of academic honesty policies.

units.why: "Be thoughtful about when this tool is useful. Don't use it if it isn't appropriate" asks students to judge when AI is appropriate and to remain the decision-maker, so P32.
units.anchor: Don’t use it if it isn’t appropriate for the case or circumstance.

units.why: "Any work written, developed, created, or inspired by artificial intelligence (AI) is considered plagiarism and will not be tolerated" classifies AI-involved work as plagiarism, so P36.
units.anchor: is considered plagiarism and will not be tolerated

units.why: "in the realm of education and learning, this kind of technology does not belong" sets a blanket ban for the course, so P01 (default prohibition).
units.anchor: in the realm of education and learning, this kind of technology does not belong

units.why: "the use of AI robs us all of the opportunity to learn from our experiences and from each other" explains the ban by lost practice and learning, so P41.
units.anchor: the use of AI robs us all of the opportunity to learn
units.frag_start: This is because the use of AI

units.why: "this class is specifically a space for learning how to improve our writing. AI simply cannot do that learning for us" gives a course-specific skill-building reason, so P41.
units.anchor: AI simply cannot do that learning for us.
units.frag_start: In a nutshell, college is a place

units.why: "any use on graded work/ work for credit will be considered a violation of the academic misconduct policy" is a graded-work ban enforced as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: will be considered a violation of the academic misconduct policy
units.frag_start: Note that this instructor has set

units.why: "This would be an appropriate statement for a class in which the course outcomes have been compromised by use of the technology" says a ban suits courses whose outcomes AI undermines, i.e. the course decides: P04 rather than P01 because it is guidance to instructors on choosing.
units.anchor: an appropriate statement for a class in which the course outcomes have been compromised
units.frag_start: This would be an appropriate statement
units.frag_end: would happen in a writing course).

units.why: "you are not authorized to use artificial intelligence engines, software, or artwork generating programs ... to produce work for this class EXCEPT" sets a ban unless permitted, so P01 with restrict.
units.anchor: you are not authorized to use artificial intelligence engines, software, or artwork generating programs
units.frag_start: Generally speaking, you are not authorized

units.why: "EXCEPT on assignments that I have identified and for which you will have received significant guidance" allows AI only on instructor-named assignments, so P04 (per-assignment permission).
units.anchor: EXCEPT on assignments that I have identified
units.frag_start: Generally speaking, you are not authorized

units.why: "I will provide more information about the specific assignment when the time is appropriate" says expectations will be communicated assignment by assignment, so P09.
units.anchor: I will provide more information about the specific assignment

units.why: "You may not, however, construe this limited use as permission to use these technologies in any other facet of this course" limits permission to the named assignments, so P11 (permission does not carry over).
units.anchor: construe this limited use as permission to use these technologies in any other facet

notes: Single library guide, not an official provost policy. Units inside the three example statements are coded as written in those statements (student-facing), although the guide presents them as templates for faculty. One unit is UNCOVERED.
